name: Crucible Investiture Ceremonial Robe — General Assembly
description:
Crucible's investiture ceremonies are industrial in their scale and blunt in their symbolism, and the General Assembly robe reflects that without apology. The garment is a full-length overrobe in Crucible's signature iron-gray, constructed from a heavy wool-analog that has been bonded with a thin layer of fire-resistant substrate — a practical accommodation for ceremonies that often take place on or adjacent to active manufacturing floors. The chest bears a large embroidered Crucible emblem in copper-analog thread, and rank indicators along the left sleeve mark the wearer's division and seniority level within the corponation. The robe is unisex in cut and sized generously to fit over standard augmentation rigs and basic chrome.

These robes are worn by all assembly-level employees invited to investiture ceremonies — promotions to supervisory rank, new facility openings, production milestone commemorations. They are issued at the door, worn for the duration of the ceremony, and returned. The fact that thousands of identical robes exist, that you are one of thousands wearing one, is not a flaw in the design. In Crucible culture, collective identity is the point.
cultural_context: Crucible workers who have attended multiple investiture ceremonies sometimes develop a strong attachment to the robe as an object, even though they never own one. The ceremony it represents — being present, being counted as part of the collective — carries real weight in Crucible's corporate culture.
story_hooks: A character is handed a General Assembly robe at the door of what they were told was a production milestone ceremony. The rank indicators on the sleeves around them are far above anything they've seen at this tier of event. Something larger is being announced.

Someone has managed to keep a Crucible investiture robe rather than returning it. Crucible has not come looking. That either means the oversight system failed, or they want the robe to be kept for a reason.

A character attending their first Crucible ceremony puts on the robe and realizes, standing among thousands of identical gray figures, that they cannot find their coworkers. The ceremony begins before they do.

physical_description.visual_profile: A severe, architectural silhouette — floor-length overrobe with a commanding presence. Boxy shoulders, straight lines, no ornamentation beyond the bold copper emblem at the chest. Reads as industrial formality: a uniform disguised as ceremony wear.
physical_description.fit: Generously cut and deliberately oversized to accommodate standard augmentation rigs and chrome installations. Relaxed through shoulders and torso, with a straight drop to ankles. Designed for layering and accessibility, not flattery.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy wool-analog bonded with a thin fire-resistant substrate. Durable synth-blend that mimics natural wool's weight and drape while meeting industrial safety codes.
physical_description.texture: Densely woven with a subtle nap finish. Matte surface with minimal sheen. Feels substantial and slightly stiff when new; softens with repeated wear. The fire-resistant layer creates a subtle papery quality just below the surface.
physical_description.color_scheme: Iron-gray as the dominant color — a neutral, utilitarian tone that reflects Crucible's manufacturing identity. Copper-analog thread for the emblem and rank indicators adds warm metallic contrast without breaking the austere palette.
physical_description.closures: Full-length front opening secured by heavy-duty magnetic snaps spaced down the length of the robe. Quick-release system designed for rapid dressing and undressing in ceremony logistics.
distinctive_features: Large embroidered Crucible emblem centered on the chest in copper-analog thread — approximately 20cm diameter, highly stylized industrial iconography
Rank indicators running vertically along the left sleeve — small copper bars and hash marks corresponding to division and seniority level
Reinforced inner lining at shoulders and upper back to support augmentation harnesses
Hidden venting panels at sides for thermal regulation under layers of chrome
No personalization: every robe is identical, bar rank markings
Notched collar with functional button loop (magnetic snap beneath)
Wrist cuffs designed to sit above or below augmentation sleeve interfaces
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 corporate formal wear — expensive enough to signal legitimacy and investment, but utilitarian enough to broadcast function over status.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn exclusively at Crucible investiture ceremonies by assembly-level employees summoned to witness promotions, facility openings, and production milestones. Signals collective belonging, earned presence, and participation in corporate ritual. The robe is issued and reclaimed — you never own it, but wearing it means you've been counted.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when first issued. After ceremony use, may show minor creasing and wear. The fire-resistant substrate can develop a faint scuff patina from repeated handling. Well-maintained because thousands of other robes depend on the same upkeep infrastructure.

image_prompt: A tall, angular neo-noir model with visible augmentations (chrome shoulder joint, neural port on neck) wearing a floor-length iron-gray wool ceremonial robe with oversized shoulders and a massive copper-embroidered Crucible emblem at the chest. Rank indicators glow faintly along the left sleeve in warm copper. The model stands in a brutalist industrial warehouse setting with exposed steel beams and manufacturing equipment visible in soft focus behind. Cool, overcast lighting casts shadows across the robe's heavy weave. The image conveys authority without vanity, collective belonging without individuality. Moody, severe, professional. Mannequin alternative: robe draped on a sleek chrome stand with rank sleeve positioned toward camera. --ar 2:3 --v 6
